A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TS-Reasoner and provide readable methods, results, figures, tables, and appendices. Despite substantial rewriting and reorganization, retained material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original TimeSeriesExam evaluations, constrained forecasting and diagnostic experiments, and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results and additional component ablations, generalization experiments, and backbone comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated handling of repeated plans: v3 completes execution without further intermediate feedback, whereas v4 describes prompting reflection and explicit selection of the best buffered model. The decomposition architecture and four operator families remain intact.

E1.justification: V4 adds causal discovery with qualitative directional constraints and stock-price future-volatility prediction (Table 2), plus a search-frequency forecasting example (Figure 1). These introduce distinct task requirements beyond the retained TimeSeriesExam, electricity, weather, and numerical-prior causal tasks. Renaming existing tasks predictive/diagnostic does not itself expand coverage.

E2.justification: The GPT-4o, o1, and DeepSeek comparators are substantively revised from generated-code execution to CodeAct agents with execution feedback, explicitly evaluated in Table 1 and Figure 4. ReAct remains. Figure 1 also introduces an o4-mini-high comparison.

E3.justification: V4 replaces the described generate-code/execute baseline procedure with iterative CodeAct feedback capped at six interaction turns. New experiments introduce GPT-4o versus LLaMA 3.1 70B configurations and transfer protocols using one added causal example or no task-specific volatility example. Existing benchmark metrics and dataset statistics are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds sequential feedback/operator ablations (Figure 6), backbone robustness testing (Table 4), qualitative-constraint and domain generalization tests (Table 2), and classified paraphrase-ambiguity examples (Table 5). These substantially extend v3's error analyses and paraphrase evaluation; the existing error-case figures are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports standard deviations for retained diagnostic F1 and causal-accuracy results, previously presented as plot points. Forecasting standard deviations in Table 1 are mainly rounded from four decimals to two. No repeated-run confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerous baseline results are replaced under the CodeAct setting. For example, Table 1's GPT-4o maximum-load prediction without covariates changes from success rate/MAPE 0.55/0.2043 to 0.80/0.1607. Diagnostic error distributions also change, and new ablation, transfer, and backbone results appear. These reflect changed settings, rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The original decomposition and output equations remain. Section 3.3 adds explicit mathematical definitions for execution outcomes, feedback updates, quality-maximizing model selection, and scored buffer memory. This is limited formal development without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a new multi-step inference paradigm, a program-executing TS-Reasoner with specialized operators and feedback, a benchmark, and advantages over general-purpose LLMs. Domain-oriented branding and reordered contribution statements do not materially change these central claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive interpretations separating feedback's contribution to execution success from operators' contribution to inference quality, arguing reduced dependence on backbone reasoning capacity, and explaining transfer to qualitative constraints and new tasks. It also removes v3's explicit qualification that new task types may require additional operators and demonstrations.

D1.justification: V4 discloses AgentScope, temperature 0, top_p 1, and A40 hardware, and rewrites the prompt with an operator-signature example. It removes v3's illustrative synthetic-data code and unified-evaluator pseudocode. Dataset statistics, the operator catalog, and the sample-data URL remain available within the PDF.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts substantially toward domain-specialized agents, adding discussion of SWE-agent, HoneyComb, CRISPR-GPT, and AdaPlanner. V3's direct discussion and citations of time-series reasoning work by Merrill, Chow, and Xie/ChatTS disappear, alongside several other time-series and reasoning references.

P1.justification: V4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental narrative. Dataset construction moves into Appendix A, appendices are reorganized, and task terminology becomes predictive/diagnostic. The title and author ordering also change.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the introductory task-example figure with a forecasting plot, removes the dataset-generation diagram, adds an ablation figure and three tables, and adds average columns to Table 1. Retained diagrams and plots are recolored, resized, or regrouped, within a different document layout.

improvement.justification: Feedback-enabled baselines and new component, backbone, and transfer tests strengthen evidence missing from v3. Gains are tempered by removed code examples, misleading covariate labels in Figure 6 and Table 4, and Table 1's inconsistent o1 average MAPE of 0.1268 despite component values of 0.1433–0.1672. These reporting weaknesses limit the net improvement.
